structural: The text has one structural obligation. `NodeContents::format` must be a trait method with the signature `fn format(&self) -> String` on `pub trait NodeContents: Send + Sync`. Presenting the retained contents, using the same observation as `fingerprint()`, and needing no further reads are behavioral clauses.

An alternative declaration such as `fn format(&self) -> Result<String, _>` or `fn format(&mut self, ctx: &Resources) -> String` would violate the prescribed signature. A trait without the method would violate it too. So the signature is a real structural obligation.

The root `crates/trust-but-verify/src/domain.rs#trait[NodeContents]/fn[format]` meets it. It declares `fn format(&self) -> String;` inside `trait NodeContents: Send + Sync` (`crates/trust-but-verify/src/domain.rs#trait[NodeContents]`). Its doc comment says all resource reads and fallible preparation happen when loading contents. That matches the no-further-reads obligation, which only the implementors can fulfil.

The other clauses are observable behavior, so they need no implementation root. They are the use of the same observation as `fingerprint()` and the completion of formatting without reads or fallible preparation. The fallible-preparation clause is partly reflected in the signature, because `String` is returned rather than a `Result`. Tests cover the remaining behavior.

I found no other root that needs a reference.

behavioral: Both marked tests cover the obligations of `requirements.sdk.graph.node_content.format`.

Obligations I derived:
1. `format()` presents the retained contents as agent text.
2. It uses the same observation that `fingerprint()` describes.
3. It uses only the retained value. It does no further resource reads and needs no fallible preparation.

Coverage:
- `crates/trust-but-verify/tests/contracts.rs#fn[identities_remain_stable_and_fingerprinting_uses_the_supplied_snapshot]` reads a snapshot while the node holds "before" and asserts `format()` returns "before".
  - It then changes the underlying resource to "after". `format()` still returns "before", so formatting uses the retained value and not the live resource.
  - It asserts that the read log is exactly `[1]`, so `format()` triggered no extra read.
  - It asserts that `content.fingerprint()` equals the snapshot fingerprint (value "before"). That ties `format()` and `fingerprint()` to the same observation.
- `src/sdk.rs#mod[tests]/fn[domain_formats_supplied_contents_without_resolving_a_replacement]` builds contents with `HabeasNodeContent::prepare` from an already-read `ResolvedInput`. Its file, `missing.rs`, does not exist.
  - It asserts that `format()` output contains the retained text and the file name. If `format()` re-read the file, the output could not contain that text, so the assertion passes only when everything needed for presentation is retained.
  - The test shows formatting works without resource access.

The no-fallible-preparation clause is a type-level property, because `format(&self)` returns `String`. The tests call it without any `Result` handling, which is enough.

I found no uncovered behavioral obligation and no marking gap.
